revisions.objective: Focus on CTA-level source tiling while each output thread traverses source tiles serially, distinguishing this from T3’s warp-parallel source reduction. Stage only x, y, z and mass for force calculations; treat full-record staging, including unused velocities, as a separate measured variant if explored. Use safe block-wide synchronization for partial source tiles and a grid-stride output mapping so coverage does not depend on items_per_block being available to device code. Keep shared-memory use within the configured limit, and check correctness before timing.

revisions.objective: Use controlled arithmetic ablations in the one-thread-per-target loop: compare the unchanged expression, an rsqrtf-based reciprocal-distance variant without target-mass cancellation, a target-mass-cancelled variant retaining the original sqrt/division path, and then their combination. Keep other transformations separate so the effect of each can be judged. Do not enable global fast math. Validate tolerance, finite outputs, and exact mass preservation on all required cases before comparing repeated timings.
revisions.subject: Isolated ablations of reciprocal-square-root arithmetic and target-mass cancellation

revisions.objective: Test warp-level lane-parallel source accumulation and force reduction without a CTA shared-memory source tile, keeping this distinct from T1. Handle arbitrary N, source tails, and self interaction; document the effect of strided AoS source loads and changed reduction order. Validate numerical tolerance, finite outputs, and exact mass preservation across the required cases before repeated timing.
revisions.subject: Warp-parallel source reduction without block-wide source tiling

data.shared_assumptions: The supplied baseline is correct and timed, but no per-size timings or profiling establish whether source traffic, arithmetic throughput, or launch occupancy dominates; treat all four topics as hypotheses. T1 and T3 now test contrasting mappings rather than both implicitly targeting shared source reuse. The kernel cannot read items_per_block directly, so every mapping must ensure complete output coverage using launch-visible dimensions. Preserve the single-kernel interface and require full correctness checks and confirmation on the distinct official input data before accepting any performance result.
